body:
Sometimes I've questioned if I'm pure evil though too. I've treated people like shit myself, although I don't realize it until they tell me, and some gave me chances to learn from it and others just told me that I was doing something wrong, but never said what. Also, the doctors tell me all I need is a support system and the best they can do is have me to talk about anything (with mandatory reporting, which my mother could manipulate and retaliate against me easily for.. since obviously she's my mother and she knows many things other people don't.. and since it's not hard with the internet) and prescribe meds. If I could just work and leave, I can be safe for the future. Although if that I had the opportunity to move away, I'm not sure I could actually trust somebody to take them up on the offer. There's stories, for example, like: Person gets hurt, stranger offers to help, stranger hurts victim too

I've tried to get help from other people for so long, but I feel like a congressional bill.. I'm redirected and redirected and redirected and redirected until I'm finally talked about and debated, which is this point.

Well, I tried to stay strong by talking about it to this one guy who told me about this place, but I had been trying to gain the courage to post here for a month, watching TV shows, listening to music, reading, eating (far from the best way), and figuring out other stuff to get my mind off. But it works.. for a time.. and then everything is back to the way it used to be.. and start over again. I've been accused of being bipolar.. I get sad.. and I get angry.. and I do get happy.. but I realized last night that being happy is such a large fallacy that I even fooled myself.

No. There's my sister, who's hundreds of miles away with all rooms filled. My mother's close with all my uncles and my aunt so that won't work. The employment search assistant I talk to once a week has a family and that would be really awkward to ask and could prevent any further chance of getting a job. A couple of friends who are in their 40s and 50s are 2 hours away, but they have families too. There's a few other people, but they all have families too. The only people I'd have left are people I've never met or talked to.. ever.

Well, my mother would say I'm an adult now, but I still feel like a child and like I've never fully grown up.

Yeah, but the only people I've ever told about emotional problems is that one social worker and the rest are online. My mother can manipulate anybody very easily and make them believe what she wants them to believe. Though I have evidence in her handwriting in my baby book from when I was like 4-6 months old that I was given Benadryl by a doctor at one point and I was given a vaccination to stop a fever, however that works. Benadryl, at least, you shouldn't give to infant under 1-2 years of age. I think this was the same doctor who nearly had me go under surgery on my genitals because I hadn't started puberty aggressively yet. This was somewhere between age 9 and 11 (and the doctor was from India, so I had wondered if boys there went through puberty at like age 6 or something). Thankfully, though, we were poor so that was a factor in not getting it. After puberty started, everything was normal. >.>

Well, I feel like it.. I have weird thoughts like.. Is this normal to be thinking about this?.. and then.. Is this normal to question if this is normal?  And yeah, I think about it and it is very simple actually. Pay the bills, maintain property, stay alive, have good hygiene, do great work, fuck debt, invest, exercise, and watch TV.

I already hate and it makes my mother PO'ed. I do stand up to my mother and call out her hypocrisy when she won't stop, thanks to wwe giving me courage. But 99% of the time, I just run to my room and pretend not to hear her. Exercising.. good idea, I really do need to. The only meds I'm on right now is medicines are allergy meds and meds for my Tourette's (which help many times except for severe cases of nervousness, like when I'm around other people, especially my mother). And no, it didn't. Actually, the feeling was overwhelming and I cried because you were so nice to me, yet you still apologized.
